we can update $o$ directly to match the target output behavior, rather than indirectly updating $f(x)$ through the prompt."},{"point":"D2","problem":"How to measure optimizer success fairly when some target outputs may be impossible to produce via greedy decoding.","did":"They reported a normalized success rate restricted to outputs for which any run of any optimizer found a satisfactory prompt, alongside the raw success rate.","alternatives_named":[],"stated_reason":"Some failures may be inevitable because outputs may not be greedily generatable, so raw success rates understate optimizer performance.","quote":"We therefore also compute a normalized success rate: the success rate over outputs where any run of any optimizer produces a satisfactory prompt.
